questions.question: A production-inventory model chooses production $P_t\ge0$ and end-of-period stock $I_t\ge0$ for periods $t=1,\dots,T$, given demands $d_t$ and initial stock $I_0$. Which equation correctly links the stock of period $t$ to the previous one?
options: $P_t-d_t=I_t$

questions.question: A production-inventory model has balance equations $I_{t-1}+P_t-d_t=I_t$, demands $d_t$ and production $P_t\ge0$. What does the restriction $I_t\ge0$ for every period express?
options: Each period's demand is met in full on time, with no shortages
Production in a period may never exceed that period's demand
Some positive stock must be kept at the end of every period
The holding cost of a period can never become a negative cost

questions.question: A production-inventory model chooses production $P_t\ge0$ and end-of-period stock $I_t\ge0$ for periods $t=1,\dots,T$, given demands $d_t$ and initial stock $I_0$, minimizing $\sum_t(c_tP_t+h_tI_t)$ (unit production cost $c_t$, unit holding cost $h_t$) with all $c_t>0$, $h_t>0$ and no required final stock. Why does every optimal plan have $I_T=0$?
options: The balance equation of period $T$ forces $I_T=0$ for every plan
The final stock must return to $I_0$, and $I_0=0$ was assumed here
Final stock carries no holding cost, so the model is indifferent
Each unit left at the end costs $c_t$ and holding but serves no demand

questions.question: A production-inventory model chooses production $P_t\ge0$ and end-of-period stock $I_t\ge0$ for periods $t=1,\dots,T$, given demands $d_t$ and initial stock $I_0$, linked by $I_{t-1}+P_t-d_t=I_t$. Once $I_0$ and all production quantities $P_1,\dots,P_T$ are fixed, what can be said about $I_1,\dots,I_T$?
options: They remain free and are chosen to make holding costs smallest
Each equals $P_t-d_t$, the surplus of its own period only
They are fixed too, computed period by period from the balance
They are fixed only if every period's production equals demand

questions.question: A planner builds a production-inventory model with balance equations $I_{t-1}+P_t-d_t=I_t$ but the problem description says nothing about the stock $I_0$ available at the start. How should $I_0$ be handled?
options: Leave $I_0$ as a decision variable for the LP to choose freely
Fix a value, such as $I_0=0$, as a stated modelling assumption
Ignore $I_0$, since it affects only the holding cost of period 0
Ignore $I_0$, since only total demand over all periods matters

questions.question: A production-inventory model has $I_0=0$, demands $d_1=100$, $d_2=90$ and production $P_1=120$, $P_2=80$, with $I_{t-1}+P_t-d_t=I_t$. What is the end-of-period stock $I_2$?

In a production-inventory model with $I_{t-1}+P_t-d_t=I_t$, period $t$ starts with $I_{t-1}=35$ units in stock, demand is $d_t=60$, and the plan wants $I_t=15$ units left at the end. How much must be produced in period $t$?

In a production-inventory model, unit production costs are $c_1=30$, $c_2=34$, $c_3=41$ and holding a unit from the end of one period to the next costs 5. Which way of producing a unit for period-3 demand is cheapest?
options: In period 2, at 39 per unit
In period 1, at 35 per unit
In period 1, at 30 per unit
In period 3, at 41 per unit

questions.question: A two-period production-inventory model minimizes $\sum_t(c_tP_t+h_tI_t)$ (unit production cost $c_t$, unit holding cost $h_t$) with $c_1=10$, $c_2=14$, $h_1=h_2=2$, $I_0=0$, $d_1=30$, $d_2=50$. What is the cost of the plan $P_1=50$, $P_2=30$?

A production-inventory model covers $T=6$ months with production $P_t$ and end-of-month stock $I_t$ for each month, a given initial stock $I_0$, and one balance equation per month. How many decision variables and balance equations does it have?
options: 13 variables and 7 equations
6 variables and 6 equations
12 variables and 6 equations
12 variables and 5 equations

questions.question: A production-inventory model chooses production $P_t\ge0$ and end-of-period stock $I_t\ge0$ for periods $t=1,\dots,T$, given demands $d_t$ and initial stock $I_0$, minimizing $\sum_t(c_tP_t+h_tI_t)$ (unit production cost $c_t$, unit holding cost $h_t$) under $I_{t-1}+P_t-d_t=I_t$ and capacities $P_t\le u_t$. Period 3 has $d_3>u_3$ and the lowest $c_t$. What does every feasible plan do?
options: Leave the excess $d_3-u_3$ unmet, since this is cheaper than storing
Make up the excess $d_3-u_3$ in period 4, after the demand period
Produce $d_3$ in period 3 anyway, since $c_3$ is the lowest cost
Produce part of the period-3 demand earlier and hold it in stock

questions.question: A production-inventory model minimizes $\sum_t(c_tP_t+h_tI_t)$ (unit production cost $c_t$, unit holding cost $h_t$), where $I_t$ is the stock at the end of period $t$ after demand $d_t$ is met. On which units is the holding cost $h_2$ charged?
options: On all units produced during period 2, sold or not
On the units still in stock at the end of period 2
On the units sold to meet the demand of period 2
On the average stock held during period 2

questions.question: A production-inventory model chooses production $P_t\ge0$ and end-of-period stock $I_t\ge0$ for periods $t=1,\dots,T$, given demands $d_t$ and initial stock $I_0$, minimizing $\sum_t(c_tP_t+h_tI_t)$ (unit production cost $c_t$, unit holding cost $h_t$) with all costs positive. The model is extended with the requirement $I_T\ge50$ for the next season. What holds for every optimal plan?
options: It ends with exactly $I_T=50$ units, the required level
It still ends with $I_T=0$, since stock is costly
It ends with some $I_T\ge50$; any such value is optimal
It does not exist, since final stock is never optimal

questions.question: A production-inventory model has $c=(20,26,31)$, holding cost 4 per unit at the end of each period, demands $d=(10,20,30)$, $I_0=0$ and no capacity limits. What is the minimum total cost?

A production-inventory model has $I_0=0$, capacity $P_t\le50$ in each of periods 1 to 3 and demands $d=(30,45,70)$, with $I_t\ge0$. What is the smallest end-of-period stock $I_2$ that any feasible plan can have?

In a three-period production-inventory model minimizing $\sum_t(c_tP_t+h_tI_t)$ (unit production cost $c_t$, unit holding cost $h_t$), a feasible plan ends with $I_3=15$ unneeded units, while $P_3=40$, $c_3=20$ and $h_3=2$. By how much does the cost fall if $P_3$ is reduced by 15?

A production-inventory model chooses production $P_t\ge0$ and end-of-period stock $I_t\ge0$ for periods $t=1,\dots,T$, given demands $d_t$ and initial stock $I_0$, capacities $P_t\le u_t$ and $I_t\ge0$. Which condition is necessary and sufficient for the model to have a feasible plan?
options: $I_0+u_1+\dots+u_T\ge d_1+\dots+d_T$ for the whole horizon
For every $t$: $u_t\ge d_t$, so each demand is producible
For every $t$: $I_0+u_t\ge d_t$ in that period alone
For each period $t$: $I_0+u_1+\dots+u_t\ge d_1+\dots+d_t$

questions.question: A production-inventory model minimizes $\sum_t(c_tP_t+h_tI_t)$ (unit production cost $c_t$, unit holding cost $h_t$) with $c_t,h_t>0$, balance $I_{t-1}+P_t-d_t=I_t$ and $P_t\ge0$, but the modeller forgets the restriction $I_t\ge0$. What does the optimal solution then do?
options: Match each period's demand, since the balance still forces it
Become unbounded, as negative stock can grow without limit
Stay as before, as negative stock would only add holding cost
Produce nothing and let the stock become ever more negative

questions.question: A production-inventory model has initial stock $I_0=25$, demands $d=(40,30,50)$ and must end with $I_3\ge10$. Every plan satisfies $I_{t-1}+P_t-d_t=I_t$ and $I_t\ge0$. What is the smallest possible total production $P_1+P_2+P_3$?

Over three periods, unit production costs are 10, 12 and 14, demands are 20, 40 and 60, there is no initial stock, at most 50 units can be made per period, and every unit in end-of-period stock costs $h\ge0$ in each period. For which $h$ is the plan $P=(50,50,20)$ optimal?
options: For all $h$ in $[0,2]$
For all $h$ in $[0,4]$
For all $h$ in $[0,1]$
For all $h$ in $[0,\infty)$
